title: Add dissector for World of Warcraft World (WOWW) protocol
description:
Works on https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/17481 and was discussed in https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/11398.

# This PR:

* Fixes the WOW protocol (only one W) using ASCII encoding instead of UTF-8. [1](https://wowdev.wiki/CMD_AUTH_LOGON_CHALLENGE_Client), [2](https://wowdev.wiki/CMD_REALM_LIST_Server)
* Adds the WOWW (World of Warcraft World) protocol on TCP port 8085 as a continuation of the WOW protocol. [1](https://wowdev.wiki/World_Packet), [2](https://wowdev.wiki/Login)

## The WOWW Protocol

The protocol is used by Blizzard for communication between a game client and their "world" server for gameplay and has been used since the start of World of Warcraft (public release 2004). It is a continuation of the WOW protocol currently in Wireshark which is used for login.

The protocol defaults to TCP port 8085 [1](https://wowdev.wiki/World_Packet) [2](https://wowdev.wiki/Login) [3](https://www.ownedcore.com/forums/world-of-warcraft/world-of-warcraft-emulator-servers/wow-emu-questions-requests/747465-why-using-3724-8085-server-possibility-using-another-ports.html), and has only been used on that port as far as I know both officially and for emulation.

The protocol consists of messages between the client of server with [1](https://wowdev.wiki/World_Packet):

* A 16 bit size field that contains the size of the data and the opcode field.
* A 16 or 32 bit opcode field, that contains information 1 out of 1060 opcodes. The field size is 16 bits when the server sends to the client, and 32 bits when the client sends to the server. This will be important for session key deduction.
* A variable sized data field, that depends on the opcode.

The header (size and opcode) fields are "encrypted" using a session key negotiated during the WOW protocol. The encryption works by XORing the unencrypted byte with a byte of the session key, and then adding (with overflowing) the previous encrypting value. Decryption is done by subtracting the last encrypted value and XORing with the session key.

[More info on header encryption/decryption](https://gtker.com/implementation-guide-for-the-world-of-warcraft-flavor-of-srp6/#world-packet-header-encryption).

## Session Key Deduction

Because the client opcode field is 32 bits but there are no opcodes greater than 1060 (0x424), the two most significant bytes will always be 0. This means that every message the client sends leaks two bytes of the session key. Depending on how many actions the client takes before logging in, this usually means that the session key can be fully deduced before the client makes their first character movement.

There are other techniques that could be used for deducing the session key (potentially in fewer messages), such as:
* Complete knowledge of the size and opcode of the first encryted message always sent by the server.
* Restricted possibility of sending opcodes outside of the character screen opcodes before logging into the server.
* Knowledge that certain opcodes can only be sent by the server, and others only by the client.

However these are not included now since they would add significant complexity and add minimal value since the full session key is very rapidly deduced anyway.

## Notes about versions

This implementation is fully compatible with version 1.12.x.

commits_data.title: WOWW: Add protocol
commits_data.message:
WOWW: Add protocol

The protocol is a continuation of the WOW protocol occuring between the
world server and the client (as opposed to the login server and the
client).

The first two opcodes are unencrypted and perform setup for the
encryption.
The encryption was setup in the WOW protocol through SRP6.
Using the session key for encryption like this is not part of the SRP6
protocol.
All other opcodes are encrypted using the session key, which will need
to be deduced first.
